# Baja Racing at Cornell

> Baja Racing at Cornell (also known as Cornell Baja Racing) is a student engineering
> project team at Cornell University that designs, builds, and races a new off-road
> vehicle every year for the SAE Collegiate Baja Design Series. Founded in 2003, the team
> first competed in 2005 and is one of the Student Project Teams in Cornell Engineering.
> It has 60+ members across six subteams.

Site: https://baja.mae.cornell.edu/
Contact: baja@cornell.edu (general) | rp665@cornell.edu (sponsorship)
Location: Ithaca, New York, USA
Parent organization: Cornell University (Cornell Engineering)
Status: Registered student organization of Cornell University

## Competition record

- 10 first-place overall finishes and 30 top-five finishes since first competing in 2005.
- 2025 season (car TG21): 1st Place Overall at all three SAE Baja competitions —
  Marana, Arizona (May); Mechanicsville, Maryland (June); Gray Court, South Carolina (October).
  This earned Iron Team status, the first for Cornell Baja since 2014.
- 1st Place Mike Schmidt Memorial Award in 2025 and 2014; additional podium finishes for
  that award in 2024, 2023, 2018, 2016, and 2015.
- Full year-by-year results for every car from 2005 (LC01) to 2026 (TG22):
  https://baja.mae.cornell.edu/timeline

## Subteams

Six subteams: Drivetrain, Transmission, Suspension, Frame, Brakes, and Business.

- Drivetrain — the driveline from the transmission out to all four wheels: front and rear
  gearboxes and casings, bevel box, propshaft, driveshafts, wheel hubs, and the four-wheel-drive
  system; structural and thermal analysis validated with an engine dynamometer and on-car telemetry.
- Transmission — the custom continuously variable transmission (CVT), tuning shift
  behavior and gear ratios for torque and top speed.
- Suspension — handling characteristics and custom suspension geometry for off-road terrain.
- Frame — the vehicle's chassis and roll cage.
- Brakes — the braking system.
- Business — competition logistics, the SAE Business Presentation event, sponsor relations,
  fundraising and budgeting, this website, apparel and merchandise, and the #girlsofbaja
  initiative celebrating female engineers on the team.

## How to join

Recruitment runs each fall only; there is no spring cycle. There are two applications, one for
upperclassmen and one for first-year and transfer students, and each asks the applicant to pick
either the mechanical track or the business track. You may apply to only one track.

- Open to any Cornell undergraduate, from any school or major, including transfer students.
  Graduate students are not eligible.
- No prior experience is required. New members complete a comprehensive onboarding program led
  by a dedicated onboarding director, including training sessions covering CAD and individual
  components.
- Process: a written screening, then two in-person interviews before a panel of team members,
  then offers. Interviews are usually held on weekends and run 20-30 minutes.
- Roughly 20-25 new members join each year: 16-18 mechanical first-years, 1-2 mechanical
  sophomores, 2-3 business first-years, and 1-2 business sophomores.
- Members are placed onto a specific subteam in their sophomore year.
- Deadlines are firm; late applications are not accepted.
- First-year members who want to attend travel to 2 of the team's 3 competitions, fully covered.

Current dates and application links: https://baja.mae.cornell.edu/apply

## About the competition

SAE Baja competitions run over four days and combine static events (design presentation,
cost report, sales presentation, technical inspection) with dynamic events (maneuverability,
acceleration, hill climb or tractor pull, a competition-specific special event, and a
four-hour wheel-to-wheel endurance race worth the most points). Every vehicle in the series
uses the same 10 HP engine, so reliability and power efficiency drive the design.
There are three North American competitions each year, each with over 100 teams.
